name: NYC Marathon 2026 — 10-Week Experienced Runner Build
description: Compressed marathon-specific plan for an experienced runner returning from a running break, with prior 50K/50-mile training history and a sub-4:00 NYC Marathon goal.

ultra_history: Previous peak training volume approximately 55 mi/week
athlete_context.current_status: Returning after a period away from running

primary_influences: Daniels-style separation of easy running and quality
philosophy.adaptation_for_athlete: Faster mileage progression than a novice return because of prior high-volume and ultra history, with workout performance and recovery used as the governor rather than a rigid 10% mileage rule.

weeks.notes: Treat 24 miles as complete. No retroactive restructuring.

checkpoint.name: Checkpoint 1 — 3 x 1 mile
checkpoint.signal: Can approximately 8:30/mi threshold work be completed in control, with relaxed form and quick recovery?
checkpoint.green: Could have done another rep; pace feels controlled.
checkpoint.yellow: Can hit pace but it feels harder than expected.
checkpoint.red: Straining to hit pace, form deteriorates, or recovery is poor.

workouts.title: Recovery
workouts.details: Easy recovery.

workouts.title: Threshold
workouts.details: 2 mi easy, 4 mi threshold at 8:30-8:45/mi, 3 mi easy/cooldown.

workouts.title: Easy aerobic
workouts.details: Easy/aerobic.

workouts.title: Marathon pace introduction
workouts.details: 2 mi easy, 4 mi at 9:05-9:10/mi, 1 mi easy.

workouts.title: Long run
workouts.details: Easy. Optional final 3 mi around 9:30-9:45/mi if feeling excellent.

checkpoint.name: Checkpoint 2 — 4 mi marathon pace
checkpoint.signal: After 3 easy miles, does 9:05-9:10/mi feel like controlled marathon effort rather than a race?
checkpoint.green: Relaxed, controlled, and could continue several more miles.
checkpoint.yellow: Can hold pace but it feels closer to tempo effort.

workouts.title: Recovery
workouts.details: Easy recovery.

workouts.title: Threshold intervals
workouts.details: 2 mi easy, 5 x 1 mi at 8:20-8:40/mi with 2 min easy recovery, cooldown.

workouts.title: Easy aerobic
workouts.details: Easy/aerobic.

workouts.title: Marathon pace
workouts.details: 2 mi easy, 5 mi at 9:05-9:10/mi, 1 mi easy.

workouts.title: Long run with steady finish
workouts.details: First 14 mi easy; final 6 mi around 9:20-9:40/mi. Do not force marathon pace.

checkpoint.name: Checkpoint 3 — 20-mile durability test
checkpoint.signal: Can 20 miles be completed with good fueling, reasonable mechanics, and manageable recovery afterward?
checkpoint.green: Finishes controlled and resumes normal training quickly.
checkpoint.yellow: Completes it but needs several days to recover.
checkpoint.red: Major breakdown, severe soreness, or inability to resume training normally.

workouts.title: Recovery
workouts.details: Easy recovery.

workouts.title: Marathon-specific threshold
workouts.details: 2 mi easy, 3 x 2 mi at 8:40-8:55/mi with 3 min easy recovery, cooldown.

workouts.title: Easy aerobic
workouts.details: Easy/aerobic. Add 1-2 easy miles here if choosing the 58-mile version.

workouts.title: Key marathon pace test
workouts.details: 2 mi easy, 6 mi at 9:05-9:10/mi, 2 mi easy.

workouts.title: Long run
workouts.details: Easy. Optional final 4 mi at marathon effort only if exceptionally fresh.

checkpoint.name: Checkpoint 4 — Key 6-mile marathon pace test
checkpoint.signal: Can 6 mi at 9:05-9:10/mi be run after substantial accumulated training without it feeling like a race?
checkpoint.green: Controlled, repeatable pace; feels comfortably hard; could continue 5-6 more miles.
checkpoint.very_green: Feels strong enough that another 5-6 miles at similar effort seems realistic.
checkpoint.yellow: Pace is achievable but requires substantial concentration and feels around 7.5/10.
checkpoint.red: Cannot sustain target pace without significant strain.

weeks.notes: Peak workload week. Use 56 miles if fatigue is accumulating; 58 only if recovery is excellent.

workouts.title: Final marathon-specific progression
workouts.details: Miles 1-8 at 10:15-10:30; miles 9-14 at 9:45-10:00; miles 15-20 at 9:10-9:20 if controlled. Do not force the final segment.

checkpoint.name: Checkpoint 5 — Final 20-mile progression
checkpoint.signal: Can marathon-ish effort be produced after 15 miles without a major deterioration?
checkpoint.green: Final 5-6 mi around 9:10-9:20 with controlled mechanics and effort.
checkpoint.yellow: Can finish around 9:20-9:30 but 9:10 feels too hard.

checkpoint.name: Checkpoint 6 — Taper MP check
checkpoint.signal: Does marathon pace now feel easier than it did during the peak weeks?
checkpoint.green: MP feels controlled and noticeably easier with reduced fatigue.
checkpoint.yellow: MP remains controlled but not especially easy.

weeks.notes: Stop trying to gain fitness through volume. Preserve fitness and eliminate fatigue.
